MonkeyHub starts the Runtime (main), shares its refusals (errors) and embeds its wire shapes (api.dto); it reads a project in process only through the Runtime's declared read API (#519): ProjectBinding and ReadToken, the event log, the runtime status, the document and work-copy readers and the Board page export. Everything else in project_runtime is reached over the Hub's forwarding path, so the Runtime can change its insides without the Hub following them. The skills installed on this machine (skill_library.installed, S-1) are read the same way: the skill folders and what a person allowed are this machine's, not a project's, and listing them reads those folders only and touches no project.
ProjectBinding and ReadToken are the Runtime's public read API, which MonkeyHub opens in process (#519): the binding holds no web framework, and the app-state glue beside it is structural.

The HTTP layer calls the application layer, never the reverse: api imports application, and application imports no route, no DTO and not the conditional-read middleware. The schemas of the records application reads back (the working position, a render request, a recipe's graphics, a Study's research) are application's own, and api.dto builds on them (#519).
A DTO shapes the wire and never reaches back into a route; only create_app (project_runtime.main) mounts the routes.
